land.text: the Medici grand duchy at Gian Gastone's death on 9 July 1737: Florence, Pisa, Livorno, Arezzo, Siena and the Maremma

predecessors.note: 'On 9 July 1737, Gian Gastone died; the last male Medici of the grand ducal line.' Don Carlos was 'forced to give up the Tuscan succession by the Treaty of Vienna (1738)' and Francis Stephen of Lorraine became heir. The grand duchy itself dates from 1569 (rename event in the republic-of-florence dossier); Cliopatria's Grand Duchy of Tuscany row starts only in 1797.

land.text: the Grand Duchy as it stood in 1859, joined to Modena and Parma on 8 December 1859

successors.note: 'Merged into the United Provinces of Central Italy: 8 December 1859'; 'Annexed to Sardinia: 22 March 1860' after a referendum. The United Provinces have no Cliopatria row and no dossier yet.

correction.text: the grand duchy as the Medici left it in 1737, to 1796; Don Carlos's claim set aside by the Treaty of Vienna (1738)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1737-1796: Cliopatria has no Tuscany between its Republic of Florence row (ends 1737) and 1797. The state continues under the House of Lorraine on the Medici territory: Cliopatria's Florence 1734 shape, 19,852 km2, against the infobox 'Area (1852): 21,710 km2' (ratio 0.91, the difference being Lucca and the Presidi added later).

correction.text: the grand duchy of 1737, unchanged in 1797 and 1798

keyframe_review.note: 1,032 km2 around 10.3E 44.0N for 1797-1798: a thousand km2 near Lucca and the Garfagnana, 21 times too small for a grand duchy of about 21,700 km2 (infobox 1852) and not the Tuscan heartland (Florence, Pisa, Siena). Replaced by the Medici-Lorraine extent. The page does not cover 1796-1798 (no neutrality, no Livorno occupation).

correction.text: holds only to 21 March 1801; from then the Kingdom of Etruria draws the land

keyframe_review.note: The same 1,032 km2 for 1800-1802. The Grand Duchy was 'abolished ... 21 March 1801' and 'replaced by the Kingdom of Etruria' (Treaty of Aranjuez), so the shape is wrong in size and in years: Tuscany proper for 1800 to 21 March 1801 only, thereafter the kingdom-of-etruria dossier.

correction.text: belongs to the Kingdom of Etruria, created from the Grand Duchy by the Treaty of Aranjuez

keyframe_review.note: 985 km2 for 1803-1805, when there was no Grand Duchy: the land was the Kingdom of Etruria (21 March 1801 to 1807). The shape to use is Cliopatria's Kingdom of Etruria (23,128 km2 maximum), dossier kingdom-of-etruria.

correction.text: Etruria to 1807, then annexed to France on 30 May 1808; the 1809 'Grand Duchess of Tuscany' ruled for France

keyframe_review.note: 1,032 km2 for 1806-1813. Etruria was 'to be annexed' by the Treaty of Fontainebleau (27 October 1807) and 'on 30 May 1808, Etruria was formally annexed to France'; in 1809 Napoleon put his sister at the head of the government 'with the title of Grand Duchess of Tuscany' as a French dependency. No independent grand duchy in these years: kingdom-of-etruria to 1807, then the First French Empire.
New keyframe 1814: 'Re-establishment: 30 May 1814'; 'Ferdinand III resumed his rule'. The land is the Medici-Lorraine extent; the Congress of Vienna adds the Presidi and Piombino in 1815.

union.text: the State of the Presidi on the Tuscan coast

correction.text: Tuscany as restored: the Medici-Lorraine state of 1737 with Piombino and the State of the Presidi, ceded in 1815; Lucca joins on 17 December 1847 and the Lunigiana domains go to Modena and Parma in 1847

keyframe_review.note: 938 km2 for 1815-1847, a sliver of the Garfagnana; the real state is about 21,000 km2 (infobox 21,710 km2 for 1852, with Lucca). The Congress of Vienna 'ceded the State of Presidi and the Principality of Piombino to a restored Tuscany' ('Granted to Tuscany: 1815'). Replaced by the extent below; Lucca (17 December 1847) and the Lunigiana domains are in the ledger. Elba is not on the pages opened.

24,632 km2 for 1848: Tuscany with Lucca ('Reversion to the Grand Duchy of Tuscany: 17 December 1847') against the infobox 21,710 km2 (1852), ratio 1.13. The shape is the only one of Cliopatria's six that is the grand duchy.

correction.text: the grand duchy of 1848 to its end in 1859

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1849-1859: Cliopatria's row ends in 1848 but the grand duchy lives to 1859 (deposition 16 August 1859, merger 8 December 1859). The 1848 shape is kept unchanged: Massa-Carrara and Lunigiana changes after 1847 are not on the pages opened.

region.text: the Tuscan state the Medici left

ledger.note: 9 July 1737: the Medici line ends and Tuscany passes to the House of Lorraine. 'On 9 July 1737, Gian Gastone died; the last male Medici of the grand ducal line'; infobox 'End of Medici rule: 9 July 1737'; Francis Stephen of Lorraine became heir after the Treaty of Vienna (1738). The page names Tuscany, not a frontier.

region.text: the whole grand duchy, now the Kingdom of Etruria

ledger.note: 21 March 1801: the Grand Duchy is abolished and replaced by the Kingdom of Etruria. Infobox 'Abolished during the Napoleonic Wars: 21 March 1801'; 'The Grand Duchy was then dissolved, and replaced by the Kingdom of Etruria' (Treaty of Aranjuez).

30 May 1814: the Grand Duchy is re-established. Infobox 'Re-establishment: 30 May 1814'; 'Ferdinand III resumed his rule, and died in 1824'. Between 1808 and 1814 the land had been French (Etruria 'formally annexed to France' on 30 May 1808; Napoleon's sister styled Grand Duchess of Tuscany from 1809).

1815: Piombino is granted to Tuscany. Infobox 'Granted to Tuscany: 1815'; 'In 1815 it was absorbed into the Grand Duchy of Tuscany'. The principality had been 'Annexed by French-controlled Lucca: June 23, 1805' as the Principality of Lucca and Piombino.

region.text: the State of the Presidi on the Tuscan coast

ledger.note: 1815: the State of the Presidi passes to Tuscany. The Congress of Vienna 'ceded the State of Presidi and the Principality of Piombino to a restored Tuscany'; the year and the 9 June 1815 date are those of the Congress's Final Act (Duchy of Lucca page, infobox 'Congress of Vienna: 9 June 1815'). The Presidi had been Etruria's since 1801 (state-of-the-presidi dossier).

region.text: the Lunigiana domains ceded to Modena (Vicariate of Fivizzano)

ledger.note: 1847: Tuscany gives up its Lunigiana domains. In the year Lucca was annexed, 'Tuscany in turn ceded its Lunigiana domains' to Modena (the Vicariate of Fivizzano) and to Parma (Pontremoli); Pietrasanta and Barga were retained. The page gives no month; both places are the researcher's reading of 'Lunigiana domains'.
1847: Pontremoli goes to Parma. The page: Tuscany ceded its Lunigiana domains and 'Pontremoli went to Parma'; no month on the page.

region.text: the Duchy of Lucca, formed 'out of the former Republic of Lucca' in 1815

ledger.note: 17 December 1847: the Duchy of Lucca reverts to Tuscany. Infobox 'Reversion to the Grand Duchy of Tuscany: 17 December 1847'; Charles abdicated on 5 October 1847; the Tuscany page: 'In 1847, in application of the 1844 secret Treaty of Florence, Leopold II annexed the Duchy of Lucca'.

region.text: the grand duchy, left to the republicans

ledger.note: February 1849: the Grand Duke flees and republicans take Tuscany. 'In February 1849, Leopold II had to abandon Tuscany to republicans.' A rebel regime of less than a year, so no rebel dossier.

region.text: the grand duchy, restored with Austrian help

ledger.note: April 1849: the grand-ducal government is restored. Leopold II page: 'In April, the municipal council usurped the powers of the assembly and invited him to return'; 'the Austrians entering Florence' on 25 May; 'On the 28th of July, Leopold himself returned.' The Grand Duchy page: 'It was only with Austrian assistance that Leopold could return to Florence.' [Reviewer eu-20-a, 2026-10-31: month added and the event moved after the February loss; source changed from the Grand Duchy page, which gives no date.]

16 August 1859: the House of Habsburg-Lorraine is deposed. Leopold II 'abandoned Florence for Bologna' on the evening of 27 April 1859, abdicated in favour of Ferdinand IV on 21 July, and 'the House of Habsburg-Lorraine was formally deposed by the Tuscan National Assembly on 16 August 1859'. The state continues under a provisional government until December.

region.text: the Grand Duchy, merged into the United Provinces of Central Italy

ledger.note: 8 December 1859: Tuscany joins Modena and Parma in the United Provinces of Central Italy. 'Merged into the United Provinces of Central Italy: 8 December 1859'; annexed to Sardinia on 22 March 1860 after a referendum.

wars.name: Napoleonic wars in Tuscany (1799-1814)
wars.outcome: A Provisional Government was created by the French army in spring 1799; the Grand Duchy was dissolved by the Treaty of Aranjuez (21 March 1801) into the Kingdom of Etruria, which the Treaty of Fontainebleau (27 October 1807) annexed to France on 30 May 1808; the grand duchy was re-established on 30 May 1814.
wars.note: Not on the page: the French occupation of Livorno in 1796 and the neutrality of Ferdinand III; the date the 1799 provisional government ended.

wars.name: Tuscan revolution of 1848-1849
wars.outcome: Leopold II sanctioned a liberal constitution in 1848, left Tuscany to republicans in February 1849 and came back with Austrian help.

wars.name: Second Italian War of Independence (Tuscany 1859)
wars.outcome: Leopold II left Florence on 27 April 1859, abdicated on 21 July, was deposed on 16 August; Tuscany joined the United Provinces of Central Italy on 8 December 1859 and was annexed to Sardinia on 22 March 1860.
wars.note: No fighting in Tuscany is on the page; no zone.

certainty.note: The long-settled Medici-Lorraine frontiers; the Lunigiana and Garfagnana enclaves and exclaves are not delineated on the pages opened.
No grand duchy: Kingdom of Etruria, then France; kept so the certainty covers the dossier's years.
Frontiers fixed by the Congress of Vienna (9 June 1815) and the 1844 Treaty of Florence (1847); the Tuscan frontier with Lucca disappears on 17 December 1847.

notes: Cliopatria row 'Grand Duchy of Tuscany' 1797..1848 (six shapes): five of them (1,032, 1,032, 985, 1,032, 938 km2) lie near Lucca and the Garfagnana (bbox about 10.0-10.5E, 43.9-44.2N), never the Tuscan heartland, and cannot be the grand duchy; only the 1848 shape (24,632 km2) is. They look like a mislabelled Lucca polity. The dossier therefore starts at 1737, where the republic-of-florence dossier hands over, with new keyframes for 1737-1796, 1814 and 1849-1859, and marks the others wrong. State with a gap: abolished 21 March 1801 (Kingdom of Etruria 1801-1807, French 1808-1814), re-established 30 May 1814; kept as one dossier; the Etruria years are in kingdom-of-etruria. Page budget 5 pages (3 opened): not settled are the Lorraine period 1737-1796 (no territorial event on the page; the page has no list of grand dukes, so no ruler strip), the French occupation of 1796 and 1799 (the page has only the spring 1799 Provisional Government), the Pietrasanta/Barga/Lunigiana border before 1847, Elba, the post-1847 Massa-Carrara changes, the 1849 republic's dates, the 1859 provisional government (April to December). Piombino's page does not mention Elba. Needs a dossier: duchy-of-lucca (1815-1847, counterpart of the 1847 gain; also the Lucca Principality of 1805-1814), united-provinces-of-central-italy (1859-1860, successor), principality-of-lucca-and-piombino (counterpart of the 1815 Piombino gain, successor listed by republic-of-lucca), the Tuscan republicans of 1849 (under a year, not a rebel dossier). Gazetteer names needed: places 'Piombino', 'Orbetello', 'Fivizzano', 'Pontremoli' (the region Lunigiana is absent too). The 1815 Presidi event leans on the Tuscany page for the cession and on the Lucca page for 9 June 1815, which it does not otherwise cite. The infobox area (21,710 km2, 1852) agrees with the Medici-Lorraine shape plus Lucca, Piombino and the Presidi (about 20,600 + 1,100).
